items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to creating an exception to school busing requirements in the city of New York for restoration of past services
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S6027

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend
the education law, in relation to creating an exception to school
busing requirements in
the city of New York
for restoration of past services

PURPOSE:
This bill creates an exception to school busing requirements in the
city of New York for restoration of past services.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:
Section 1 amends paragraph c of subdivision 1 of section 3635 of the
education law.
Section 2 is the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:
In May of 2010 the New York City Department of Education announced
that it would end yellow school bus service for over 4,000 7th and
8th grade school children city-wide. Approximately two-thirds of the
students affected by this decision (nearly 3,000) who attend 47
schools are Staten Islanders. Prior to September of 2010 variances
had been granted to 70 schools where the options with respect to
public transportation are limited.
This situation severely impacts Staten Island due to limited
mass-transit options. The variances were issued for 18 years until
they were abruptly discontinued.

This legislation seeks to address this dangerous situation by amending
the education law to grant cities with a population of 1 million or
more an exemption from the like circumstances clause in Section 3635
(1) (c) of the law. An exemption would allow the city to restore the
yellow bus service on Staten Island to its pre-September 2010 status.
Recently, a judge ruled that the like circumstances clause of the
education law would bind the city to provide additional busing over
the entire city. According the New York City Department of Education,
this would create a significant burden on the City's education
budget. This bill would ease some of those concerns expressed by the
New York City Department of Education with respect to like
circumstances.

From a safety standpoint, 7th and 8th grade school children should
have the option of riding the yellow school bus to and from school.
Speeding vehicles, lack of sidewalks and in some cases children being
forced to cross four lanes of traffic to reach a city bus, not only
causes anxiety and fear, but is extremely treacherous. In one heart
breaking case, a child was killed when crossing several lanes to
catch her city bus home. Cost saving measures cannot take priority
over the safety and well being of children. This bill aims to restore
yellow school bus service to these young children.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
New bill.


FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
